text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Kenya Seed Company is blamed by Agricultural Development Corp for the spread of a fungal maize disease.
- Four people die in fierce fighting over grazing rights in Tana River district.
- Opposition politicians urge President Daniel arap Moi to invite Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila to the Nairobi Great Lakes meeting scheduled for Wednesday.
- A former cabinet minister engages heavily armed gangsters in fierce gunfire after they carried out a spate of robberies at a neighbouring village.
- Shocked Kenyans react angrily to increasing cases of lesbianism in the country.
- Parliament resumes business on Tuesday and is scheduled to debate the controversial Public Accounts Committee Report.

- Kimani Rugendo, the FORD-Asili candidate for the just-ended Langata by-election demands that results be nullified and winner Raila Odinga barred from contesting future polls over serious offences during the exercise.
- North Eastern Provincial Commissioner Maurice Makhanu reveals that some of the most notorious, heavily armed bandits terrorising area residents reside in local refugee camps.

- The circumstances under which the Kenya Ports Authority paid a Canadian firm 245 million shillings ($4.45 million) for the refurbishing of dockside cranes before completion is questioned as more reports of contentious payments emerge.
- Tanzania attains a record foreign exchange reserve position of 270 Tanzania billion shillings ($450 million) attributed to strong export growth and donor support.

- The front-runner in the bid for a 30 billion Uganda shillings ($27.5 million) project to rehabilitate Uganda's Mulago Hospital could be derailed by a confidential report from a Kenyan engineering firm questioning their ability to undertake the assignment.
